name: Multi-layer Beer-Lambert Raycasting with Ambient Occlusion and Shadowing
definition: A volume rendering technique that splits the ray into segments (layers) based on accumulated opacity thresholds. It computes color and alpha using Beer-Lambert law parameters (emission/absorption) for each segment, while applying ambient occlusion (AO) from neighboring samples and shadow sampling along a specific direction. It supports Level of Detail (LoD) and cubemap-based indirect lighting.
summary: Multi-layer Beer-Lambert Raycasting with Ambient Occlusion and Shadowing is a GPU volume rendering technique that splits rays into layers for separate compositing while applying ambient occlusion and shadowing.
